title: Protesters arrested and tree-sitter targeted during border wall construction
seoTitle: Nogales border wall tree protection protest

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against the environmental destruction caused by the construction of a new border wall in the San Rafael Valley.
tea.want: They want to halt border wall construction and protect ancient cottonwood trees along the U.S.-Mexico border.
tea.changed: Oct 10: Mexican authorities and U.S. agents removed a wooden platform supporting an activist perched in a tree.

summary: Activists and local residents have been camping in the San Rafael Valley near Nogales, Arizona, since June to protect ancient cottonwood trees from being destroyed for the construction of a new 30-foot border wall. The demonstrations escalated when federal agents moved in to clear the protest camp, resulting in multiple arrests and confrontations. While the final major cottonwood tree on the U.S. side was removed in early October, activists continued their opposition, with at least one protester maintaining a tree-sit across the border in Mexico. Organizers criticised the federal government for rushing construction and damaging the local ecosystem, whereas U.S. Customs and Border Protection defended the project, stating that preconstruction surveys found no migratory bird nests and emphasizing the environmental hazards caused by unauthorized border crossings.
demands: Protect ancient cottonwood trees along the border
response: U.S. Customs and Border Protection stated that environmental resources are respected during construction, preconstruction surveys showed no bird nests, and that unauthorized crossings create substantial environmental damage. Fisher Sand & Gravel and Mexican authorities assisted in operations against tree-sitters.

updates.text: Federal agents moved in to clear the protest camp and detained several activists as the last cottonwood tree was cut down.
Mexican firefighters and U.S. agents removed a wooden platform supporting a tree-sitting protester just across the international border.
